chapter.name: Limits and Derivatives
chapter.blurb: This chapter is the first introduction to calculus. Starting from the average velocity of a falling body, it builds the idea of a limit (with left and right hand limits), the algebra of limits, limits of polynomial, rational and trigonometric functions, and the standard limits of (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) and (sin x)/x. It then defines the derivative as a limit, finds derivatives from first principle, and develops the sum, product and quotient rules with the derivatives of polynomials and trigonometric functions.

scope_in.item: Compute average velocity over a time interval for s = 4.9t^2 and similar distance functions, and estimate the instantaneous velocity from average velocities over shrinking intervals on either side
Interpret instantaneous velocity (the derivative of the distance function) as the slope of the tangent to the distance-time curve, the limit of slopes of chords
Explain the limit of f at a as the value f(x) approaches as x tends to a, read it from a table of values or a described graph, and recognise that it need not equal f(a)
Find left hand and right hand limits of piecewise-defined and modulus functions and decide whether the limit exists (it exists only when the two coincide)
State and use the algebra of limits: limit of a sum, difference, product, constant multiple and quotient (denominator limit non-zero)
Evaluate limits of polynomial functions by substitution, and of rational functions by substitution or, in the 0/0 case, by cancelling the common factor; recognise when the limit does not exist
State, prove and apply lim (x -> a) (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) = n a^(n-1) for positive integer n, and use the remark that it holds for rational n when a is positive
State the sandwich theorem and the inequality cos x < (sin x)/x < 1, and explain how they give lim (x -> 0) (sin x)/x = 1
Use lim (x -> 0) (sin x)/x = 1 and lim (x -> 0) (1 - cos x)/x = 0 to evaluate trigonometric limits, including by a substitution that makes the variable tend to 0
State the definition f'(a) = lim (h -> 0) [f(a + h) - f(a)]/h, compute a derivative at a point from it, and interpret it as the slope of the tangent (limit of chord slopes)
Find the derivative function from the first principle for polynomial and simple rational functions, and use the notations f'(x), dy/dx, d/dx f(x), D(f(x))
State and apply the sum, difference, product (Leibnitz) and quotient rules for derivatives
Use d/dx (x^n) = n x^(n-1) (integer n, as used in the exercises) to differentiate polynomials term by term and products and quotients of polynomials

Recall and derive the derivatives of sin x, cos x and tan x (first principle) and of cot x, sec x, cosec x (quotient rule), and differentiate sums, products and quotients involving them, rewriting sin 2x or sin(x + a) by an identity first

concepts.name: Intuitive idea of the derivative: average and instantaneous velocity
concepts.description: Average velocity over shrinking time intervals for the falling body s = 4.9t^2, the instantaneous velocity as the value these approach, and its meaning as the slope of the tangent to the distance-time curve.
concepts.idea: The velocity at one instant cannot be found from a single distance and time; it is the value approached by average velocities over smaller and smaller intervals around that instant.
concepts.rule: Average velocity between t1 and t2 = (s(t2) - s(t1))/(t2 - t1). The instantaneous velocity is the limit of these as the interval shrinks, and equals the slope of the tangent to the distance-time curve.
concepts.example: For s = 4.9t^2 the average velocity over [1.99, 2] is 19.551 m/s and over [2, 2.01] is 19.649 m/s, so the velocity at t = 2 lies between them.

concepts.name: Limit of a function: left hand and right hand limits
concepts.description: The limit as the value a function should assume near a point, left and right hand limits read from tables, graphs and piecewise definitions, and when a limit exists.
concepts.idea: The limit of f at a is the value f(x) approaches as x approaches a; it depends on values near a, not on f(a) itself.
concepts.rule: lim (x -> a) f(x) exists only if the left hand limit and the right hand limit at a coincide; the common value is the limit. The limit and f(a) may differ, and one may exist without the other.
concepts.example: For f(x) = 1 (x <= 0), 2 (x > 0): the left hand limit at 0 is 1, the right hand limit is 2, so the limit at 0 does not exist although f(0) = 1.

So f(x) = 3x^2 - x + c for any constant c, for example f(x) = 3x^2 - x. Check: [f(1 + h) - f(1)]/h = [3(1 + h)^2 - (1 + h) - 2]/h = (5h + 3h^2)/h = 5 + 3h, which tends to 5 as h -> 0.
s: Obtains f'(x) = 2ax + b and the conditions b = -1, 2a + b = 5
Gives a valid quadratic with a = 3, b = -1
Verifies f'(1) = 5 from the definition

s: States that (u/v)' is not u'/v' and that the quotient rule must be used

questions.q: Choose two different non-constant polynomials u(x) and v(x) of your own. Find the derivative of their product by the product rule, and verify your answer by first multiplying out uv and differentiating term by term.
questions.a: For example u = x^2 + 1 and v = 3x - 2, so u' = 2x and v' = 3. Product rule: (uv)' = 2x(3x - 2) + (x^2 + 1)(3) = 6x^2 - 4x + 3x^2 + 3 = 9x^2 - 4x + 3. Expanding: uv = 3x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x - 2, whose term-by-term derivative is 9x^2 - 4x + 3. The two agree. (Any correct pair earns full marks.)
s: Chooses two non-constant polynomials and applies (uv)' = u'v + uv' correctly
Expands uv and differentiates term by term
Shows that the two results agree

concepts.name: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
concepts.description: The derivatives of sin x, cos x and tan x from first principle, those of cot x, sec x and cosec x by the quotient rule, and derivatives of sums, products and quotients involving trigonometric functions.
concepts.idea: The first principle applied to sin x uses the formula for sin A - sin B and the limit of (sin h)/h; every other trigonometric derivative then follows from the product and quotient rules.
concepts.rule: d/dx (sin x) = cos x, d/dx (cos x) = -sin x, d/dx (tan x) = sec^2 x. Functions such as sin 2x are differentiated by first rewriting them with a trigonometric identity.
concepts.example: d/dx (sin^2 x) = d/dx (sin x . sin x) = cos x sin x + sin x cos x = 2 sin x cos x = sin 2x.

questions.q: Find the derivative of f(x) = (sin x + cos x)/(sin x - cos x) and simplify it.
questions.a: u = sin x + cos x, v = sin x - cos x, so u' = cos x - sin x and v' = cos x + sin x. u'v - uv' = (cos x - sin x)(sin x - cos x) - (sin x + cos x)(cos x + sin x) = -(sin x - cos x)^2 - (sin x + cos x)^2 = -(1 - 2 sin x cos x) - (1 + 2 sin x cos x) = -2. Hence f'(x) = -2/(sin x - cos x)^2.

Simplifies the numerator to -2 using sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1
